recognize_zh: 與中央的小淋巴球相比，紅血球體積偏小（小球性），可見少數橢圓形、淚滴狀及口形樣紅血球，但整體大小相當一致、蒼白區不太擴大；這種「輕度小球性、紅血球形狀輕微異常而無明顯缺鐵變化」的抹片符合β-地中海型貧血帶因者，但單靠形態無法確診。
features: Red cells appear small relative to the nucleus of the central small lymphocyte, suggesting microcytosis
Relatively uniform red cell size (little anisocytosis) with mild poikilocytosis: occasional elliptocytes, teardrop-like and stomatocyte-like cells
Central pallor present but not markedly expanded; hypochromia is mild at most
No definite target cells, basophilic stippling or nucleated red cells in this field
Single small mature lymphocyte with condensed chromatin and scant blue cytoplasm; occasional platelets
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows red cells that appear microcytic relative to a small lymphocyte, with relatively uniform size and mild poikilocytosis including occasional elliptocytes and teardrop-like forms. Hypochromia is mild, and target cells and basophilic stippling are not conspicuous in this field. White cells and platelets are unremarkable in this limited view. The findings are nonspecific but compatible with thalassemia trait; correlation with red cell indices (low MCV with high RBC count) and hemoglobin HPLC showing increased HbA2 is needed for a diagnosis of beta-thalassemia trait.

ddx.vs: Iron deficiency shows more anisocytosis (high RDW), pronounced hypochromia and pencil cells with a low RBC count and low ferritin, whereas thalassemia trait has uniform microcytes with a high RBC count.
Morphology is essentially identical; separation requires a normal HbA2 on HPLC and alpha-globin gene deletion testing.
ACD is usually normocytic or mildly microcytic with low serum iron but normal-to-high ferritin and normal HbA2.
Normal red cells are about the size of a small lymphocyte nucleus; confirmation of microcytosis requires the MCV rather than visual comparison.
